root_cause.text: The NFC subsystem's nfc_unregister_device() holds device_lock while calling rfkill_unregister(), which acquires rfkill_global_mutex, while rfkill_fop_write() holds rfkill_global_mutex then acquires device_lock via nfc_dev_down(), creating an ABBA deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description explicitly shows the deadlock chain: Thread A (rfkill_fop_write) locks rfkill_global_mutex then waits for device_lock; Thread B (nfc_unregister_device) locks device_lock then waits for rfkill_global_mutex. The patch moves rfkill_unregister() and rfkill_destroy() outside the device_lock critical section to break this inversion.

The patch moves rfkill_unregister() and rfkill_destroy() outside the device_lock critical section to break this inversion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local variable to hold the rfkill pointer so that the function can properly clean up the rfkill device when unregistering an NFC device.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration `struct rfkill *rfk = NULL;` inside the `nfc_unregister_device` function.
intent_record.how: The new variable is initialized to NULL; this does not alter current behavior by itself but prepares the function to later use the pointer for rfkill operations such as unregistration or destruction.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy outside the device lock to prevent potential deadlock.
intent_record.what: Moved rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy calls from inside the locked region (device_lock/unlock) to after the lock is released, using a local pointer to hold the rfkill object and setting dev->rfkill to NULL while still holding the lock.
intent_record.how: The code now saves the rfkill pointer to a local variable, clears dev->rfkill under lock, then releases the lock, and only then performs rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy if the pointer is non-NULL. This avoids holding the device lock during potentially blocking operations.

grouping_result.intent: Add a local variable to hold the rfkill pointer so that the function can properly clean up the rfkill device when unregistering an NFC device.
Move rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy outside the device lock to prevent potential deadlock.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds a local variable to hold the rfkill pointer, which is likely a preparatory step to restructure the cleanup order and resolve the ABBA deadlock between device_lock and rfkill_global_mutex.
The group's changes directly address the ABBA deadlock by moving rfkill_unregister and rfkill_destroy outside the device lock, which breaks the lock ordering cycle described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This call to rfkill_unregister is made while holding device_lock, which creates a lock ordering violation with rfkill_global_mutex, leading to an ABBA deadlock when rfkill_fop_write locks rfkill_global_mutex then device_lock via nfc_dev_down.
This call to rfkill_destroy is also made while holding device_lock, contributing to the same lock ordering violation as part of the vulnerable code path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call to rfkill_unregister is made while holding device_lock. Since rfkill_unregister acquires rfkill_global_mutex, and rfkill_fop_write (which locks rfkill_global_mutex then device_lock via nfc_dev_down) creates a lock ordering violation, this statement contributes to the ABBA deadlock.

This call to rfkill_destroy is also made while holding device_lock, following rfkill_unregister. It is part of the same critical section that creates the deadlock condition, as it is within the same locked region that violates lock ordering.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
NFC: RFKILL support

All NFC devices will now get proper RFKILL support as long as they provide
some dev_up and dev_down
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit be055b2f89b5842f41363b5655a33dffb51a8294
Author: Samuel Ortiz <sameo@linux.intel.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 11 11:52:20 2013 +0200

    NFC: RFKILL support
    
    All NFC devices will now get proper RFKILL support as long as they provide
    some dev_up and dev_down hooks. Rfkilling an NFC device will bring it down
    while it is left to userspace to bring it back up when being rfkill unblocked.
    This is very similar to what Bluetooth does.
    
    Acked-by: Marcel Holtmann <marcel@holtm
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces rfkill_unregister in nfc_unregister_device() but calls it before device_lock is acquired (line 893-895), so the deadlock condition (holding device_lock while calling rfkill_unregister) is not present. Hence no vulnerability exists in this commit.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit be055b2f89b5 introduces rfkill support. In nfc_unregister_device(), rfkill_unregister() is called before device_lock is acquired (lines added after 'id = dev->idx;' and before the device_lock block). Since the root cause requires holding device_lock while calling rfkill_unregister, this code does not have that ordering. The vulnerable ABBA deadlock is not present; only the B->A path exists via nfc_rfkill_set_block calling nfc_dev_down which takes device_lock. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is absent.
